key_insight: A multimodal speech-based LLM approach that combines audio and transcripts can detect cognitive impairment more accurately and generalize better than single-modality methods.
clinical_relevance: This work supports non-invasive, privacy-preserving screening for cognitive impairment that could help identify at-risk patients earlier.
method: Extract acoustic embeddings directly from speech audio
Generate textual embeddings from automatic speech transcripts
Concatenate both modalities for downstream classification with open-source LLM-based features
evidence_signal: Evaluated on ADReSS20 and ADReSSo21 benchmarks, the framework achieved 92.4% classification accuracy and outperformed single-modality baselines with improved cross-dataset generalization.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of speech recordings and automatic transcripts, which may vary across settings and affect real-world robustness.
paper_title: Toward Generalizable Cognitive Impairment Detection with Speech-Based Multimodal Large Language Models
